payload.acceptance_criteria: a record minted by the kit after this change is refused by dor unless it carries requirements; a record without the marker is reported as owing requirements but is not refused for that alone; trigger and acceptance criteria are still required of every open record
payload.description:
## Trigger

When the definition-of-ready gate asks a record for its requirements, I want it to ask only records created after the rule existed, so I can stop refusing 341 records for content nobody could have written.

Measured 2026-09-18 over the folded ledger: all 341 open records owe requirements, 0 carry the field and 0 carry a heading to migrate from. The engine seam could not write that field until basicly-77tjvmk, so the debt was never a lapse, it was impossible. Retro-filling 341 statements would be inventing content, which is the guess you keep.

The discriminator may not be a timestamp. Section 9.5 forbids deriving anything from the clock, and there is no global ordering across records because sequence numbers are per item. So the rule binds on a marker the producer writes at create: a record minted under the rule carries it, an older one does not, and absence is unambiguous because every new record gets it.

The debt stays visible rather than being forgiven. owed still reports requirements for an unmarked record, so the board keeps showing it; only the refusal is withheld.
payload.requirements: the marker is a field the producer writes, never a clock reading and never a global sequence, because neither exists per record. No engine import, standard library only, Python 3.9 floor. No record already in the ledger is rewritten: the rule reads what is there.
